KĀLA CHAKRA · CONSCIOUS JOURNEY WITH NATURE’S RHYTHMS

Observe Nature’s rhythms, gradually arrange and align life with the evolving energy of its cycles. Reduce friction and striving against time.

1. Time Is a Living Cycle

Time is often experienced as a sequence of moments, but nature reveals another dimension: rhythm. Day and night, lunar phases, seasons and the larger movements of the heavens repeat in cycles.

Within each cycle, energy does not remain uniform. It unfolds, reaches a point of culmination, and returns through a movement of integration. Path of Time uses this cyclical view to explore the changing quality of time and our relationship with it.

2. Ascension (Arohana) and Descension (Avarohana) — Nature’s Two Movements

Every natural cycle opens, unfolds, reaches its peak and gradually returns to its point of origin.

Arohana — Ascension: Energy unfolds, expands and rises towards culmination.

Avarohana — Descension: What has reached culmination returns, integrates and takes form in the world.

A day opens with sunrise, unfolds through daylight, reaches its culmination around sunset, and descends into darkness before beginning again with the next sunrise. Each phase carries a different quality or texture of time.

When we say that we are the same as the universe—that the microcosm is the same as the macrocosm—we mean that Nature’s energy body and our own energy body work according to the same principle. If the energy body of the day moves through ascension and descension, our energy body functions in the same way.

3. The Seven Chakras — Twelve Temporal States

We use the seven chakras as a framework for describing the changing qualities of time. Each cycle moves through six ascending states, reaches Sahasrara, and then moves through six descending states.

4. Three Natural Cycles of Time

Day

Poetically, life is a story stitched together through the repetition of days. Each day is a complete cycle of awakening, activity, culmination, withdrawal and renewal—a complete cycle of ascension and descension, and a daily window for alignment.

A traditional day is divided into 30 muhurtas (24 hours), each approximately 48 minutes. To incorporate the ascension through six energy states, the seventh state at the peak, and the subsequent descension through six energy states into 30 muhurtas, we need 12 temporal states. Each state contains 2.5 muhurtas, or two hours.

Our daily wheel uses 6 AM as its anchor. 6 PM is the Sahasrara point—the culmination of the ascending movement. From 6 PM, the movement descends from Sahasrara towards Ajna.

The descending day is a movement of withdrawal and integration. The person is not disappearing; they are gradually releasing the structures, roles and engagements that were necessary during the day. What has been experienced is absorbed and integrated.

We may already have aligned with this rhythm through culture, work or other aspects of life. For example:

When we are free to arrange the day in any way, we can intuitively organise it according to our orientation.

In a spiritual orientation, for example, ashram schedules often end up being arranged in a way that is closely attuned to the ascension and descension of the day’s energy body.

If we could compress the energy and experience of our entire life into a single day, we would become the Sun: always shining.

Lunar Month

A lunar month is the time the Moon takes to revolve around the Earth.

A lunar month is divided into 30 tithis: 15 ascending (waxing) and 15 descending (waning). Dividing these 30 tithis into twelve states gives 2.5 tithis per state. Beginning after Amavasya, the cycle ascends towards Purnima and descends towards the next Amavasya.

The Moon is the mind, particularly its emotional dimension. The Moon creates waves in the mind, which moves through phases just as the Moon does. At Purnima, the mind reaches its peak; towards Amavasya, it withdraws. In the final phase, from 27.5 to 30, we have Pradosham, Monthly Shivaratri and Amavasya, all considered conducive to liberation.

Yogic culture is closely attuned to the tithi cycle. Aligning with the quality of the tithis is the easiest way for grihasthas to align with natural rhythms. Then we becomes the moon. More space to manifest and withdraw. Whatever has happened, it will be over by next amavasi.

In relation to external reality:

  • In the first quarter, while we are in the lower chakras, we might be pulled into external reality.

  • In the second quarter, we will pull reality towards us.

  • In the third quarter, we might push reality away.

  • In the fourth quarter, we will be pushed away by reality.

Yearly

A year beginning on January 1 has no relativity at all.

Our year is 12 lunar cycles.

Our yearly framework begins with the first lunar cycle after the Mahashivaratri cycle and moves through twelve temporal states. The cycle ascends from the first lunar cycle, around February–March, towards Sahasrara, reaching its peak around September–October. It then descends towards the next Mahashivaratri cycle in February–March. When Adhika Masa occurs, it is included within the corresponding chakra cycle, extending that cycle’s duration without creating a thirteenth state.

In the current arrangement of the year, the Sun’s physical northward turn occurs around December 21 (the winter solstice). Its later environmental and cultural reflection comes around January 15, at Makara Sankranti (Uttarayana). In the energetic layer, however, ascension begins after Mahashivaratri. This dissonance is more noticeable in larger cycles; in shorter cycles, such as the day and month, it is less pronounced.

If we loosely map religious festivals onto the chakra states of the year, we can see how they correspond.

5. Becoming Conscious of Nature’s Rhythm

As mentioned above, we may already have arranged many aspects of our lives around natural rhythms without consciously recognising them. Our habits, cultural practices, work, rest, contemplation and spiritual observances may carry traces of this alignment.

By making these movements visible, we can become conscious of the changing quality of each period, observe how our activities relate to the natural cycle, and reconsider how we organise our lives. The intention is not to impose another rigid schedule, but to develop a more conscious relationship with the rhythms that surround us.

6. KĀLA — The Conscious Journey with Nature

Be conscious of the changing energy of Time across daily, lunar and yearly cycles.

Path of Time makes Ascending and Descending visible, identifies the chakra state of each period, and allows us to compare the external rhythm of Nature with our own internal temporal imprint.

Its purpose is to help us understand the quality of each period, become conscious of our relationship with it, and discover a more harmonious way of living—reducing resistance between our internal rhythms and the natural world, particularly for those pursuing an inward or spiritual journey.

This was Microcosm aligns with Macrocosm.

The journey is not complete when consciousness reaches its highest point. It is complete when what has been realised can be embodied in the world. As the circuit completes, all seven centres shine together as one unified field of Chaitanya — living, awakened consciousness.

The Week — A Civilisational Cycle

A week is not a natural cycle. It is an invention of civilisation. It is a day spread into its seven densities, each carrying the quality of one of the seven planets.

It is the six days of creation and the seventh day of rest. Six days of climbing, and on the seventh day ascending towards the summit; a leap into the sky on the seventh night, followed by a descent to the ground in one night. Six days to ascend and the seventh day to jump and descend.

It is the Tower of Babel — humanity's collective attempt to reach the sky.

Yoni and Linga — Context and Content

Consider the natural cycles of Time as different Yonis — contexts in which existence unfolds. The week is the main Linga — the content that penetrates these contexts, along with personal timelines, targets and cultural benchmarks.

When we are aligned with the natural cycles, the Linga can be accommodated within any Yoni.

Its point of culmination need not be the same for everyone.

For some collective traditions, the culmination is associated with Friday, Saturday or Sunday. But for an individual seeker, it could be any day. If it is Wednesday, then Wednesday becomes their Sahasrara day.

The six days before the summit represent ascent. The Sahasrara day marks culmination, the jump and the beginning of descent through the night.

Week as an External Influence

The weekly position becomes an external influence in Energy Weather. It can be calibrated to an individual's own Sahasrara day, rather than assuming that everyone follows the same weekly culmination.

KALI SPIRAL · TRANSFORMATIVE JOURNEY THROUGH HER ALGORITHM

Be conscious of how Prakriti gathers, compresses, and reclaims the mind space after a death experience. Ride through the vortex of the past, and do not drown in the madness of contents during Purification.

1 · The Reset — A New Anchor in Time

Sometimes continuity breaks. An experience arrives after which the old way of living, seeing or understanding oneself no longer holds. It may come through an awakening after years of sadhana, a meeting or initiation with a Guru, a profound loss, a near-death experience, a psychedelic experience or some other glitch event.

Somehow, the body has survived the death of the mind!

The body continues to live, but the world that the mind once inhabited has collapsed. The old identity and its familiar meanings no longer hold together.

If a person has lived consciously through years of sadhana, with relatively few entanglements with the past, the past is light. There is little gravitational pull drawing them back. What remains is to synchronise more and more with Prakriti.

For most of humanity, however, especially in this age of explosive content and experience, the past still carries enormous gravity. Its identities, relationships, desires, fears, habits and unfinished experiences continue to pull the individual back into the old life.

Most are advised to align with a Sampradaya or Guru. Fortunate are those who find Gurus who can completely carry them. They are asked to forget the past, take a new name and begin a new life. Yet the past, which carries so much gravity, can continue to haunt them. At the same time, a new anchor point pulls them towards a different existence.

The seeker may find themselves caught in the turbulence created by the dissonance between these two anchors.

How does one make meaning of this new existence?

2 · The Journey of Reclamation — Prakriti Reclaims the Space

Nature thinks the person is dead. And she starts the process of reclaiming the space element in which the mind exists, by cutting through it with her cycles of Time.

A pattern begins to reveal itself. The past seems to rotate around the present, arranged by the cycles of Nature. Previous habits, relationships and their archetypal counterparts return in new forms. Similar stories, carrying similar energy patterns, wrap themselves around the individual again and again. New family archetypes and new structures emerge.

The mother in the house becomes Mother in the temple.

This reclamation is the burning of karma, purification, purgatory, or the passage into the black-hole singularity.

This process takes place through an algorithm of compression of Time. As the accumulated past is compressed through increasingly shorter cycles, its structures gradually lose their hold, allowing the individual to move towards a new state of existence.

The body remains, and the world that once inhabited the mind is being reclaimed by Nature.

3 · The Transformation Algorithm — Compression Through Cycles

Your previous life becomes the arms of the vortex. Its lived years, experiences, identities and accumulated impressions are drawn inward, gathered and compressed through successive cycles of Time.

First compression · Saturn cycle into Jupiter cycle

Approximately 30 years → 12 years

The 30-year Saturn cycle is compressed into the 12-year Jupiter cycle. Each Jupiter year carries approximately 2.5 years of the Saturn cycle.

  • At a Death Moment around age 30, the complete 30 years are compressed into 12 Jupiter years.
  • Above age 30, the Saturn cycle repeats. Corresponding phases across successive cycles converge into the same Jupiter-year phase. For example, at age 36, the first phase gathers ages 0–2.5 and 30–32.5.
  • Between ages 12 and 30, only the years actually lived are compressed. At age 16, for example, the compression lasts approximately 6.4 Jupiter years. Most of the descending movement is already complete.

Second compression · Jupiter cycle into Earth year

12 years → 12 lunar cycles

The 12 Jupiter years are compressed into one Earth year, represented by twelve lunar cycles beginning after Mahāśivarātri. Each lunar cycle carries the contents of one Jupiter year. Its 30 tithis represent the twelve stages of that cycle, with each stage occupying 2.5 tithis.

Third compression · Earth year into lunar month

12 months → 30 tithis

The twelve months of the previous year are compressed into one lunar month. Each group of 2.5 tithis carries the contents of one previous month.

Fourth compression · Lunar month into one day

30 tithis → 30 muhurtas

The lunar month is compressed into one day. Each muhurta carries the contents of one tithi.

Fifth compression · One day into one muhurta

30 muhurtas → 48 minutes

The complete daily cycle is gathered into one muhurta of 48 minutes.

Sixth compression · One muhurta into one kala

48 minutes → 30 kalas

Each kala represents 96 seconds.

Seventh compression · One kala into kashtas

96 seconds → 30 kashtas

Each kashta represents approximately 3.2 seconds.

4. The Existential Madness

The madness arises because compression happens both sequentially and cyclically.

At any moment, a person is being bombarded by all seven (or more) cycles of Time. Shorter cycles are created through the compression of larger cycles, while the larger cycles themselves are shaped by the repackaging of entangled karmic events from previous lives.

Initially, because of cyclical compression, the entire life energy graph of, say, 30 years cannot fit into shorter cycles like a day, and there will be striving. As sequential compression progresses over years, shorter cycles also reach completion.

These karmic knots repeat over and over, appearing through different people, relationships and circumstances. The same energy graph keeps presenting itself in new forms.

The repetition continues until the person begins to see the nature of the pattern, becomes conscious of it, and makes a deliberate choice not to travel through that same energy graph again and again.

6 · Nature of Methods Evolved Based on Rupture in Saturn Phases

Lives at the Turning Point

How the temporal position of a transformative moment may shape the teachings and methods that follow. These lives offer a way to explore the relationship between a person's turning point and the distinctive flavour of their subsequent work.

Ramana Maharshi · Age 16 · Sahasrara

His spontaneous death experience turned attention towards the source of individuality itself. His method of Atma Vichara asks the seeker to investigate the very place from which the sense of “I” emerges.

Teaching flavour: Investigation of the source of consciousness.

Mata Amritanandamayi · Age 22 · Descending Anahata

Her establishment in Krishna Bhava in September 1975 can be interpreted as descending Anahata: providing love, warmth and containment for ascending Anahata.

Teaching flavour: Unconditional love, embrace, compassion and seva.

Osho · Age 21 · Descending Anahata

His subsequent methods brought meditation together with emotional expression, celebration, relationships and the questioning of psychological repression.

Teaching flavour: Emotional release, acceptance and opening the heart.

Sadhguru Jaggi Vasudev · Age 25 · Descending Manipura

Following his experience of oneness on Chamundi Hill, his work developed into structured methods of yoga, discipline and purposeful action.

Teaching flavour: Channelling individual energy through discipline and purposeful action.

Gautama Buddha · Age 29 · Swadhisthana → Muladhara

His Great Renunciation marked the departure from desire, attachment and worldly fulfilment. His enlightenment followed later, around age 35; the two moments are distinct.

Teaching flavour: Renunciation, freedom from craving and grounding spiritual understanding in everyday life.

The chakra positions are interpretations within the Path of Time framework, not historical claims made by these teachers. Ages and events are biographical reference points; final temporal positions must be checked against the agreed calculation rules.

Different turning points. Different temporal positions. Different flavours of teaching.

7 · KALI — The Transformative Journey

Somehow, the body has survived the death of the mind!

And now Nature thinks this person is dead. She begins the process of reclaiming the space. If we can allow her to do that, we can establish ourselves as the dead — no longer holding on to the old identity, no longer resisting the process of reclamation.

But is this a glitch in Nature?

No. It is the backdoor the Mother kept open for her prodigal offspring.

What appears to be an interruption in the continuity of life may actually be a passage into another way of existing. A way to return, to be reclaimed, and to become part of the larger movement of Prakriti.

Everything is Prakriti. Everything is Mother.

Jai Ma Kali!

7th Compression: 1 kala (96 seconds) → 30 kashtas (3.2 seconds each)

One kala of 96 seconds contains 30 kashtas. Each kashta is 3.2 seconds.

Transfer Ascension and Descension into Inhalation and Exhalation

Somewhere between the 6th and 7th compression, this pendulum movement of ascension and descension comes into sync with the inhalation and exhalation of breath. With every inhalation comes the complete ascension and loading of life; with every exhalation, its descension and unloading.

Inhalation, stillness, exhalation and stillness are themselves manifestations of Spanda — the throbbing of consciousness. It is present in the heartbeat, in a thought and the spaces between thoughts, and in the Prakāśa–Vimarśa of the sense of “I am”.

As compression becomes denser, these instances of Spanda — these pulses of “I am” — are squeezed closer together. The space between them narrows until there is no interval in which to fall into contents. Experience is suspended throughout.

This is the conceptual sequence. The exact arithmetic, stage boundaries and live progression from the entered date still need to be defined and validated before the vortex can calculate a personal position.
